course_description: This course builds on student experience in general dental practice and the specialist dental disciplines. Students will continue to develop their skills and competence in history taking, assessment, recognition, diagnosis, treatment planning and aspects of management for conditions managed within the dental specialties including prosthodontics, endodontics, dentomaxillofacial radiology, oral medicine, oral surgery and orthodontics. Students will develop their clinical skills and competence in multi-disciplinary care of adults with moderately complex needs and the care of children, and gain some experience with special needs patients. To support their understanding and clinical skills students will further explore aspects of human and oral diseases, dental pharmacology and therapeutics, disability and medical compromise. Each week students will undertake approximately 9 hours of clinical patient care including provision of care, dental assisting and observations and 9 hours of competency building activities such as lectures, seminars, problem-based learning, workshops, self-directed activities and pre-clinical simulation exercises. This course assumes approximately 3 hours of self-directed learning each week.

course_aims: To continue building up students’ experience in general dental practice and the specialist dental disciplines. It also aims at further developing the students' skills and multi-disciplinary care.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate high-level comprehension and application of the scientific basis of dentistry to the practice of specialist dental disciplines.
Efficiently conduct patient histories, assessment and accurately recognise and diagnose a range of conditions commonly managed within the specialist dental disciplines.
Be able to discuss and justify diagnoses, treatment options and care plans, and procedural choices.
Design and implement oral care plans which integrate general and specialist disciplines and allow for multidisciplinary care.
Demonstrate competency in clinical exercises in a range of specialist dental disciplines.
Demonstrate competency in a range of clinical procedures for patients with moderately complex needs.
Select with justification dental materials and medicaments appropriate for use in a range of clinical procedures.
Demonstrate effective, caring and responsible interactions with patients, carers, clinical and supervisory staff and peers.
Apply the principles of sterilisation, disinfection and prevention of crossinfection to maintain a safe working environment.
Demonstrate effective, accurate and responsible verbal and written communication, including electronic patient records, with patients, carers, clinical and supervisory staff and peers.
Reflect critically on their experiential learning and be able to self assess accurately when reviewing pre-clinical and clinical performance with supervisors.
Recognise personal limitations in terms of knowledge, understanding and clinical ability, and be willing to seek advice.

assessment_details.task_description: The competency exam will be held in the scheduled preclinic session for the identified week. This is a must-pass preclinical assessment for a previously assessed tooth (endodontic plastic molar 16). Students are required to demonstrate maintained competency for endodontic treatment in a standardised molar under examination conditions. The allocated tooth is identical to the one used in a previous course (DENT3071) and therefore draws upon assumed knowledge and skills. The marking rubric will be available on Blackboard. A re-sit opportunity is available for students who do not achieve a passing standard on their first attempt. No supervised practice or revision sessions will be provided prior to this resit attempt. To pass the assessment following a re-sit, students must meet the minimum competency standard in all required components. A re-sit cannot be deferred. assessment_details.title: Treatment planning sessions: SND case presentations
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Peer assessed. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This group activity is designed to support the development of comprehensive treatment plans tailored to individual patient needs. It emphasises a deep understanding of both medical and social determinants of health, while fostering empathy and clinical reasoning. Groups will present and justify their proposed treatment plan through an oral case presentation, supported by relevant materials. Students will engage in discussion and respond to questions to demonstrate depth of understanding and professional judgement. This assessment evaluates students’ ability to synthesise clinical findings, apply relevant theoretical frameworks, and communicate well-reasoned and defensible treatment decisions within a collaborative clinical context. Further details regarding case allocation, group organisation, presentation format, marking criteria and submission requirements will be provided on the course Blackboard site. The presentation will be recorded and retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application. Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use of Generative AI tools is permitted in specific parts of this assessment task This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic, and reflective of complex clinical decision-making. While the core synthesis of your patient's treatment plan, clinical reasoning, and oral defense must be the original work of the group, you may utilize generative AI tools as a preliminary aid. Specifically, AI may be used to brainstorm general medical/social determinants of health or to help structure and proofread the text on your presentation slides. However, any AI-generated suggestions must be critically evaluated, verified against peer-reviewed dental literature, and properly referenced. The final treatment plan must reflect your group's independent professional judgement. If generative AI is used, you must include an acknowledgment section outlining which tools were used and how they contributed to your preparation. Unattributed or excessive reliance on AI that replaces student clinical reasoning will be treated as academic misconduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Interim Clinical Practice Performance
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Longitudinal, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The purpose of this assessment is to evaluate the student’s clinical performance at the interim stage and provide formative feedback to support improvement before the final clinical competence assessment at the end of semester. Course Coordinator in consultation with the MNHHS Oral Health Centre clinical supervisory team will complete a report based on student’s clinical performance during the assessment period and quality of critical self-reflections following each clinical session. See Submission Guidelines for all components that must be submitted for the interim clinical practice performance task to be assessed. Detailed assessment criteria and rubrics will be provided on Blackboard. Four domains will be assessed to an expectations met (EM) or not met (ENM) standard and mapped to the Professional competency requirements for the accreditation body for this program - The Australian Dental Council (Professional Competencies of the newly Qualified Dentist) The domains being assessed are: 1. Professionalism, Communication and Health Promotion 2. Scientific knowledge and Clinical Information Gathering 3. Critical Thinking, Diagnosis and Management Planning 4. Clinical Treatment and Evaluation To achieve a pass, the criteria are as follows: All domains are weighted equally, and the student must achieve a pass in each domain, and an overall pass. A pass in each domain will involve a student receiving 2 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark in Domain 1, and no more than one "expectation not met" (ENM) in Domains 2-4. An overall pass for the report will involve a student receiving 4 or fewer "expectations not met" (ENM) mark across the 4 domains. In addition to this, there must be NO outstanding missing information within ISOH or the relevant patient management system. This includes missed treatment items , unsigned clinical records and incomplete OPG reviews. If this is not completed to a satisfactory standard, it will be deemed a fail grade for the assessment item. Please refer to the policy titled, " Process for Managing Incomplete Clinical Records by UQ Dentistry Students". Please note: Written feedback will be provided for any areas to improve as this is formative. Students must reflect on feedback and demonstrate improvement in the latter half of the semester. ePAD records may be randomly audited by the Course Coordinator for authenticity and supervisor signatures. Any significant clinical concerns related to patient safety will be escalated immediately via clinical communication pathways and documented and taken into consideration for the assessment outcomes. There is no resubmission or resit available for this component. This is a formative assessment to enable the student to receive feedback on their developing clinical competency. Any significant clinical concerns pertaining to patient safety will be escalated via clinical communication pathways to the course coordinator and recorded on this report to be considered for the assessment outcome.
